standard.name: cohort overlap specialized to a known lower share bound

novel.justification: This is a maintained scale restriction for aggregate exposure masses, appropriate when cohort exposures have been normalized to a prespecified audited range; it is not presented as a consequence of PPML theory.

standard.name: reference-period normalization for multiplicative time effects

novel.justification: This is a maintained stability restriction on calendar multipliers, satisfied in applications whose normalized aggregate exposure index is prospectively restricted to vary by at most a factor of two; it is not implied by fixed-\(T\) asymptotics.

This maintained effect-range restriction defines the application class of bounded proportional changes, covering decreases up to one half and increases up to two hundred percent without claiming that the restriction follows from the sampling model.

Known \(\kappa\) is a maintained design condition for aggregate-Poisson experiments in which the observation-window intensity or exposure offset is calibrated and audited before outcomes are observed; an estimated-intensity experiment is a distinct unsolved extension.

definitions.name: deterministic minimax expected length
definitions.construction: \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)=\inf_{C:\,\inf_{\eta}P_{\eta,\kappa}[\theta(\eta)\in C(s,X)]\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{\eta}\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}[\ell(C(s,X))]\) over Borel deterministic interval policies \(C\).

definitions.name: randomized minimax expected length
definitions.construction: \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)=\inf_{K:\,\inf_{\eta}\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}K(s,X,\{J:\theta(\eta)\in J\})\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{\eta}\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}\int_{\mathfrak I}\ell(J)K(s,X,dJ)\) over Markov kernels \(K\) on \(\mathfrak I\).

definitions.name: all-untreated-zero restricted minimax value
definitions.construction: \(D_{\mathcal U}(\kappa)=\inf_{C:\,\inf_{\eta}P_{\eta,\kappa}[\theta(\eta)\in C(s,X)]\ge1-\alpha,\ C(s,x)=\Theta\ \mathrm{if}\ \sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal U}x_{gt}=0}\sup_{\eta}\mathbb E_{P_{\eta,\kappa}}[\ell(C(s,X))]\) over Borel deterministic interval policies \(C\).

definitions.name: finite count-box and endpoint-grid value
definitions.construction: \(D_{K,h}(\mathcal K)\) is the supremum over \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\) of the deterministic minimax value over policies that report \(\Theta\) outside \(\mathcal B_K\) and use endpoints in \(\mathcal G_h\) inside \(\mathcal B_K\), with honesty required at every observed share and nuisance value.

definitions.name: Moreau--Kastler proportional-target specialization
definitions.construction: \(\theta(\eta)=\{\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}w^0_{gt}v_{gt}\}/\{\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}w^0_{gt}\}-1=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}\{w^0_{gt}/B(\eta)\}(v_{gt}-1)\), the aggregate product-Poisson specialization of Moreau--Kastler (2025), equation (3.14).

definitions.name: Kabaila--Byrne scalar-Poisson sanity reduction
definitions.construction: Under the setup restriction \(v_{gt}=q\in[1/2,3]\) on \(\mathcal D\) with \(s,A,b\) known, \(\theta=q-1\) and \(\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}X_{gt}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\kappa qB(\eta))\); rescaling by known \(\kappa B(\eta)\) gives the ordered one-parameter Poisson-mean problem studied by Kabaila and Byrne (2001).

definitions.name: exact rational certificate input
definitions.construction: \(\iota=(T,\alpha,\kappa_-,\kappa_+,\varepsilon)\), together with any mandated \(K\) and \(h\), is encoded by binary integers and signed numerator--denominator pairs in lowest terms; validity requires \(T\ge3\), \(0<\alpha<1/10\), \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and, when supplied, \(K\in\mathbb N_0\) and \(h>0\).

definitions.name: finite continuum-certificate representation
definitions.construction: A certificate is the finite tuple \(\Gamma=(K,h,\{Q_j,A_j\}_{j=1}^J,\{R_r\}_{r=1}^R,E,W,U_\varepsilon,b_\varepsilon,\delta_{\mathrm{enc}})\). Each \(Q_j\) is a rational polyhedron in the observable coordinates \(s\) and known \(\kappa\), the closed cells have disjoint interiors and cover \(\mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K\), and \(A_j:\mathcal B_K\to\{[a,c]:a,c\in\mathcal G_h,\ a\le c\}\) is a total endpoint-grid policy table, with \(\Theta\) reported outside \(\mathcal B_K\). The rational polyhedra \(R_r\) cover every \(Q_j\) crossed with the maintained \(A,b,v\) boxes. The finite record \(E\) contains outward-rounded rational enclosures for Poisson recurrences, exponential factors, cellwise target membership, coverage, risk, and the uniform count tail. The witness \(W\) contains a rational finite nuisance support, the induced integer policy program, an integral incumbent, and a complete exact branch-and-bound tree whose every leaf is either integral or carries a checkable rational dual bound; no root-relaxation value is accepted as \(b_\varepsilon\).

definitions.name: terminating verifier acceptance predicate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\) exactly when a terminating exact-rational checker verifies: the input and every table are well formed; the \(Q_j\) cells cover all of \(\mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K\); the \(R_r\) cells cover every maintained nuisance value above those observable cells; the tables define one measurable deterministic connected-interval policy family; outward Poisson and target-membership enclosures prove cellwise coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) and worst risk at most \(U_\varepsilon\); the count-tail, endpoint, and enclosure contributions obey the declared bound \(L\tau_K+2h+\delta_{\mathrm{enc}}\); the complete integer branch-and-bound witness proves \(b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\); and the final inequalities \(b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon\) and \(0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\) follow from those checked records. Acceptance is therefore a sufficient, not sampled, proof of uniform honesty and of the stated upper--lower error budget.

definitions.name: mandatory early-kill instance
definitions.construction: For \(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}}=(3,1/20,[1/100,1/100],2,1/100,1/20)\), an admissible output must keep \(K=2\) and \(h=1/100\), give a deterministic primal policy valid for every \(s\in\mathcal S_3\), and give a complete integrality-preserving lower witness with \(0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le1/20\). A sampled-share check, a fixed-share certificate, or an unresolved linear-programming relaxation is not an admissible output.

definitions.name: finite contact-stratified certificate handle
definitions.construction: Start with exact rational input encoding and construct finitely many rational polyhedral cells in observable share--intensity coordinates and maintained nuisance coordinates. Attach a total endpoint-grid policy table to each observable cell and outward-rounded rational Poisson tail, exponential, target-membership, coverage, and risk enclosures to every verification cell. Resolve nominal-coverage and target-endpoint contacts by the fixed-profile equations \(dp_a-\kappa p_a\,dM=0\), refine undecided cells, and record a complete exact mixed-integer branch-and-bound tree with integral incumbents or rational dual bounds at every leaf. The target object is a finite certificate accepted by \(\operatorname{Verify}\), including the mandated early-kill input.

statements.statement: If \(0<\kappa\le-\log(1-\alpha)/\overline m_*\), then \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)=L\exp(-\kappa m_*)\). At each fixed \(s\), the conditional value is \(L\exp\{-\kappa m(s)\}\). Every fixed-share optimizer reports \(\Theta\) at the zero table and a singleton at every nonzero table. A globally optimal observed-share policy is characterized exactly by \(C(s,0)=\Theta\) and \(\sum_{x\ne0}P_{\eta,\kappa}(x)\ell(C(s,x))\le L\exp(-\kappa m_*)-L\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}\) for every \(\eta\). The share \(s^*\) is the unique minimizer of \(m(s)\), the associated lower-endpoint nuisance is least favorable for every optimizer, and additional least-favorable configurations occur exactly when the displayed allowance binds.
statements.justification: The theorem gives an exact minimax value and a complete optimizer description in the sparse phase where regular PPML intervals fail most severely.
statements.gap: Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005) provide duality but no multivariate-Poisson value or optimizer characterization; Kabaila and Byrne (2001) treat one scalar Poisson mean.
statements.consumer: Researchers with rare cohort-time outcomes can report the shortest uniformly honest deterministic connected interval policy and know precisely when nonzero tables permit extra length.

statements.statement: Throughout the low-intensity regime, \(\exp(-\kappa m_*)L\{1-\alpha\exp(\kappa\overline m_*)\}\le D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\le(1-\alpha)L<D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\), with the left side truncated below at zero. Moreover, as \(\kappa\downarrow0\), \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to(1-\alpha)L\), \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\to L\), and \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)-D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to\alpha L\).
statements.justification: This isolates randomization as a first-order decision resource at the zero-information boundary rather than as a numerical convenience.
statements.gap: Kabaila (2013) shows atom splitting for scalar binomial tails; no located result proves strict minimax improvement in this staggered multivariate Poisson nuisance game.
statements.consumer: Regulators and analysts can quantify the exact price of forbidding auxiliary randomization when sparse counts make one table dominate coverage.

statements.statement: In the same low-intensity regime, \(D_{\mathcal U}(\kappa)=L\exp(-\kappa u_*)\) and \(D_{\mathcal U}(\kappa)>D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\) for every \(\kappa>0\). The least-favorable share is \(s^*\); the minimizing untreated nuisance has lower-bound cohort and time masses while treated multipliers remain unrestricted.
statements.justification: The result distinguishes a defensible denominator-failure fallback from the smaller all-counts-zero event and prices its conservatism exactly.
statements.gap: Moreau-Kastler (2025) notes denominator positivity in the regular imputation workflow but does not analyze exact zero events or their minimax cost.
statements.consumer: Implementers of imputed proportional effects can decide whether forcing the full range after an untreated-zero event is worth its exact expected-length penalty.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>0\), honesty forces the zero-table interval at share \(s\) to have length at least \(\ell_0(s,\kappa)\), and \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\ge\sup_{s\in\mathcal S_T}\exp\{-\kappa m(s)\}\ell_0(s,\kappa)\). This follows from the exact constrained minimum \(\min_{\eta:\,\theta=q-1}M(\eta)=u(s)+qb_0(s)\) for \(q\in[1/2,3]\).
statements.justification: The bound extends the exact zero-atom obstruction beyond the small-intensity phase without claiming sharpness where nonzero tables matter.
statements.gap: Scalar exact-Poisson intervals exploit a single ordered count; no located bound maps the zero atom into a continuum of feasible causal ratio targets under staggered nuisance.
statements.consumer: The bound gives every numerical certificate an analytic all-intensity lower benchmark and detects implausibly short candidate policies.

statements.statement: For every compact \(\mathcal K=[\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\), count cutoff \(K\), and endpoint mesh \(h\), \(\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le D_{K,h}(\mathcal K)\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)+L\tau_K+2h\). At every fixed observed share, the finite-grid semi-infinite mixed-integer program admits a finite nuisance witness set whose integer optimum equals its continuum-nuisance optimum. Complete branch-and-bound with outward arithmetic therefore supplies a valid integer lower witness; a root linear-programming relaxation alone need not do so.
statements.justification: This separates unconditional truncation and integrality control from the genuinely hard uniform-share covering step.
statements.gap: Kabaila and Byrne (2001) give scalar exact enumeration and Schafer and Stark (2009) give convergent finite games; neither yields matching integer witnesses with an explicit outward error budget.
statements.consumer: Auditors obtain finite, reproducible lower bounds and conservative upper policies rather than sampled-grid evidence or an unreported integrality gap.

statements.statement: Fix algebraic \(s\), \(\kappa\), count cutoff, and endpoint grid. On each smooth semialgebraic target-membership and nuisance-boundary stratum, every coverage or saved-length surface for a fixed action profile has the form \(\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p_a(\eta)\), and every interior critical point satisfies \(dp_a-\kappa p_a\,dM=0\) on the stratum tangent space. Finitely many connected critical components contain every extremal value, and outward algebraic--exponential enclosures decide every strict rational coverage or risk comparison.
statements.justification: This gives concrete fixed-design traction and isolates the remaining difficulty as uniform parameterization of contacts over shares and intensity.
statements.gap: Generic real-algebraic optimization does not directly decide exponential coverage surfaces; the cancellation in the critical equations is specific to the fixed-design Poisson likelihood.
statements.consumer: Verified solvers can replace arbitrary nuisance sampling by finite critical-component enclosures at each algebraic design.

statements.statement: Does there exist a total synthesis algorithm which, for every exactly encoded rational \(T\), \(\alpha\), compact \(\mathcal K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), chooses finite \(K\) and rational \(h\) and returns a finite certificate \(\Gamma\) with \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\)? Every accepted output must consist of finitely many rational polyhedral observable and nuisance cells, total endpoint-grid policy tables, and outward-rounded Poisson tail and enclosure data; acceptance must imply a measurable deterministic connected-interval family honest for every \(s\in\mathcal S_T\), every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), and every maintained nuisance value, together with \(b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon\) and \(0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\). The lower object must be a finite-support integer program accompanied by a complete exact branch-and-bound proof, not an unresolved linear relaxation. The algorithm must also accept an output for \(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}}=(3,1/20,[1/100,1/100],2,1/100,1/20)\) with the mandated \(K=2\) and \(h=1/100\), a globally share-uniform deterministic primal, and an integer lower certificate within \(1/20\). This finite verifier guarantee strictly strengthens Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 6, which gives convergence for finite-prior Monte Carlo risk rather than deterministic termination or continuum honesty, and Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, which gives qualitative drifting-subsequence uniformity rather than a finite cover, computable enclosures, or a machine-checkable acceptance predicate.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level open content: a finite accepted proof object must replace both nuisance sampling and qualitative compactness at exact coverage contacts.
statements.gap: Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, provide finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence but no terminating continuum-honesty verifier or complete integer lower proof; Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, provide qualitative subsequence criteria but no finite polyhedral cover, outward error ledger, or decision predicate.
statements.consumer: Auditors can replay exact-rational checks and certify sparse-count confidence policies simultaneously for every observed cohort composition and calibrated intensity in the declared domain.

statements.statement: At every interior parameter, \(I_{\mathcal U}(\eta)\) is positive definite and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)\) is the semiparametric efficiency bound coefficient for estimating \(\theta(\eta)\) in the product-Poisson experiment as \(\kappa\to\infty\). The least-favorable local direction is the efficient target score obtained by projecting the treated-total score onto the orthocomplement of the untreated row-plus-time nuisance score space.
statements.justification: The explicit nuisance projection identifies the regular benchmark that exact sparse-count procedures must approach.
statements.gap: Martin (2017), Theorem 2, and Wooldridge (2023) provide regular fixed-\(T\) inference for different panel targets; neither derives this counterfactual-share ratio's exact aggregate-Poisson efficiency bound.
statements.consumer: High-volume staggered-PPML applications obtain a principled variance formula and a least-favorable direction for calibration and power analysis.

statements.statement: As \(\kappa\to\infty\), \(\sqrt\kappa D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\to C_G\) and \(\sqrt\kappa D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to C_G\). The upper bound is attained by a deterministically calibrated, clipped efficient interval with full-range output on exponentially rare fit failures; the lower bound holds along interior local submodels approaching a maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
statements.justification: The theorem connects exact sparse-count honesty to regular fixed-\(T\) PPML inference and shows that randomization has no first-order high-information advantage.
statements.gap: Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004) transfer bounded decision risks between different Poisson and Gaussian experiments; the present bridge profiles the causal nuisance and transfers connected-interval minimax length with target boundaries.
statements.consumer: Practitioners obtain a regime check showing when exact certification may be replaced, to first order, by an efficient Gaussian interval.

sampling_model.design: Condition on observed \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) and on calibrated, known \(\kappa>0\); require honesty uniformly over the entire observed-share simplex.
sampling_model.units: The observations are the fixed collection of cohort--time totals \(X_{gt}\), not an individual-level sample or a finite-population randomization.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort \(g\) is untreated for \(t<g\) and treated for \(t\ge g\); the never-treated cohort is indexed by \(\infty\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cohort share is at least \(1/(2T)\). The exposure, time-effect, and treated-multiplier boxes are separately maintained restrictions on the aggregate-Poisson experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-count inference profiles \(A,b,v\) exactly under the product-Poisson likelihood. The high-intensity bridge estimates normalized row and time effects from untreated cells and treated totals. Estimating or jointly calibrating an unknown intensity is not covered.

estimand_functional: \(\theta=H/B-1=\sum_{(g,t)\in\mathcal D}(w^0_{gt}/B)(v_{gt}-1)\), with exact honest inference defined by \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\) and \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The estimator uses the ratio of average observed and counterfactual outcomes.
Pooled canonical-link quasi-likelihood and imputation produce identical cohort-time estimates under the stated nonlinear parallel-trends model.
Fixed-effect averages are consistent and asymptotically normal with the cross section growing and fixed \(T\).
Minimax expected-measure confidence sets are characterized using Bayes--minimax duality.
Theorem 6 controls off-support maximum risk while the finite-prior Monte Carlo procedure converges to its game value.
The scalar Poisson interval cannot be shortened without lowering infimal coverage below its nominal level.
Auxiliary-uniform randomization splits binomial atoms and yields exact equi-tailed intervals.
An optimal interval is obtained for a single parameter in a discrete distribution under mean criteria.
Section 2 establishes uniform asymptotic size through behavior along qualitative drifting subsequences.
Explicit randomized mappings establish global asymptotic equivalence between positive Poisson and Gaussian experiments.

tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. Its central open theorem asks for an exact finite machine representation: rational polyhedral cells, endpoint-grid policy tables, outward-rounded Poisson enclosures, and a terminating verifier whose acceptance proves global share--intensity honesty and a complete integer lower bound. The mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), \(K=2\), and \(h=.01\) instance must close the certified gap within \(.05\).

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Schafer and Stark (2009) do not provide deterministic finite termination or continuum honesty, and Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020) do not turn qualitative drifting subsequences into a finite verifiable cover.
project_justification.niche: The nonregular object is the entire worst-nuisance expected-length frontier, with deterministic connected intervals, randomized kernels, and the all-untreated-zero restriction kept distinct under maintained aggregate-exposure boxes and calibrated known intensity.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a finite certificate format whose accepted rational data prove global coverage, a conservative upper risk, and an integrality-preserving lower bound with an explicit error ledger.

related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark and the homogeneous known-mass reduction is only a sanity check. Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Schafer and Stark (2009), especially Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, establish finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence and off-support risk control, but not a deterministic stopping rule, global continuum honesty, or a complete integer lower certificate. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, characterize uniform asymptotic size through drifting subsequences, but do not provide finite rational cells, computable outward enclosures, or a terminating acceptance predicate. The open certificate question is stated as a strict finite verified strengthening of these last two guarantees. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison without itself profiling this causal nuisance or transferring the connected-interval minimax game.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve calculations are evidence, not established results. The mandatory early-kill instance is \(T=3\), \(\alpha=.05\), \(\kappa=.01\), count box \(K=2\), and endpoint mesh \(.01\): it must produce an accepted globally share-uniform deterministic primal and a complete integer lower certificate with gap at most \(.05\). A nuisance grid, sampled-share check, fixed-share certificate, root linear-programming relaxation, or unbudgeted numerical gap does not pass. Exact real-exponential contacts may defeat naive algebraic stopping, so termination of the finite verifier construction remains the load-bearing open issue.
honest_scope: All contribution statements are to be proved. The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. An unknown or estimated intensity changes the experiment and remains unsolved. No claim is made for noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, or software-default intervals. The exact positive-intensity randomized value away from the low-count phase and the global closed-form maximizer of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) are outside the promised theorem spine unless they emerge from the certificate analysis.

seed_details.title: Contact-stratified finite certification of continuum honesty
seed_details.live_opportunity: Replace convergence of finite-support prior games and Monte Carlo risk with a terminating, outward-rounded certificate that is uniform over observed shares, compact intensity ranges, and all nuisance contacts.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is the passage from risk control on finitely supported priors to coverage over a continuum: likelihood-ratio simulation is replaced by a finite semialgebraic contact stratification and verified cellwise Poisson bounds.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing staggered Poisson proportional effects with certified mixed-integer confidence policies found no paper that covers the full observed-share simplex or preserves an integer lower witness.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Schafer and Stark because their finite-support game already converges to minimax risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their Theorem 6 leaves continuum risk controlled by an uncomputed likelihood-ratio envelope and their conclusion establishes stochastic convergence, not finite global honesty, contact resolution, or an integer lower certificate.

seed_details.title: Exact atom-dominated deterministic--randomized minimax frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, pp. 2--4; Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, pp. 8--9; bounded-normal constructions, Sections 3--4
seed_details.live_opportunity: Derive the exact low-intensity value, all deterministic optimizers, least-favorable configurations, and a strict randomized gap for a multivariate Poisson causal ratio with observed-share-dependent nuisance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is test inversion after Bayes--minimax duality: the continuous restricted-location likelihood is replaced by a common zero-count atom whose target-indexed coverage constraints force the full causal range.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for minimax expected length in multivariate Poisson panels found scalar Poisson and binomial constructions but no causal panel result comparing deterministic connected intervals with randomized interval kernels.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Evans, Hansen, and Stark because their duality covers arbitrary dominated experiments.
seed_details.rebuttal: The generic duality does not calculate the value, characterize every connected-interval optimizer, locate the worst observed share, or prove a strict deterministic--randomized gap in this nuisance experiment.

seed_details.title: Uniform Poisson-to-efficient-Gaussian minimax bridge
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, pp. 2074--2078; Theorems 1 and 3; Appendix proof of Theorem 1
seed_details.live_opportunity: Show that deterministic and randomized minimax lengths have the same high-intensity limit and derive the efficient variance after profiling normalized multiplicative nuisance.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is the experiment comparison: a nonparametric Poisson-process Haar randomization is replaced by finite product-Poisson LAN after nuisance projection, with losses transferred for connected confidence intervals and boundary targets.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing Poisson--Gaussian equivalence with staggered proportional-treatment-effect minimax intervals found regular fixed-\(T\) PPML limits but no worst-nuisance expected-length transfer.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang because finite product-Poisson experiments are simpler than their Poisson process.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their equivalence does not profile the staggered nuisance tangent space, compute the causal efficient variance, preserve bounded-target contacts, or transfer the minimax connected-interval game uniformly.

seed_details.title: Exact positive-intensity randomized optimum
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction and Sections 2--3, especially the auxiliary-uniform construction \(Z=Y+V\)
seed_details.live_opportunity: Determine the exact randomized minimax value beyond the zero-information limit by splitting multivariate Poisson atoms subject to nuisance-uniform coverage.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is scalar monotone-tail inversion; it becomes a nuisance-indexed convex game over count-table atoms without a total order.
seed_details.destination_search: The located randomized exact-interval literature treats scalar binomial or Poisson parameters and does not solve the multivariate staggered nuisance game.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Stevens randomization because an auxiliary uniform variable splits every discrete atom.
seed_details.rebuttal: Atom splitting gives feasible procedures but does not solve the least-favorable nuisance game or determine the exact minimax value.

seed_details.title: Exact penalty of forcing the full interval on all-untreated-zero tables
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, pp. 2--5; Section 3.2.2, equation (3.14); Conclusion, pp. 40--42
seed_details.live_opportunity: Separate denominator fragility in the imputed proportional-effect workflow from the smaller all-counts-zero event and quantify the minimax length penalty of a forced fallback.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is the denominator argument after equation (3.14): asymptotic positivity is replaced by exact finite-count event geometry for untreated cells.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for exact finite-count inference on the counterfactual-share ratio found Fieller and scalar rate-ratio intervals but no observed-share-uniform staggered-panel penalty theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate because the probability of an all-zero Poisson block is the exponential of minus its total mean.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability calculation is elementary, but identifying the global worst observed share and proving the restricted minimax value require the causal nuisance geometry; alone, however, this remains too narrow for the kernel.

seed_details.title: Multivariate exact enumeration with monotone endpoint control
seed_details.anchor_location: Abstract and algorithmic construction, Canadian Journal of Statistics 29, pp. 99--106
seed_details.live_opportunity: Lift ordered scalar-Poisson endpoint enumeration to finite count boxes for connected intervals with continuous multiplicative nuisance and observed shares.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is ordering acceptance regions by one scalar count; the panel experiment requires enumeration of interval actions on a partial order and verified optimization over nuisance cells.
seed_details.destination_search: No located exact-Poisson interval algorithm handles multidimensional nuisance, a causal ratio target, and global share uniformity.
seed_details.red_team: A routine Cartesian-product extension of the scalar endpoint algorithm should suffice.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cartesian products do not preserve connectedness for the ratio target and do not certify coverage across nuisance and target-endpoint contacts.

seed_details.title: Drifting-sequence characterization of coverage contacts
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction and Section 2 general results on drifting subsequences
seed_details.live_opportunity: Characterize every limiting coverage failure as a sequence approaching nominal-coverage, nuisance-boundary, or target-endpoint strata, and make the characterization effective.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is subsequence extraction: qualitative asymptotic subsequences are replaced by finite exact-Poisson contact cells with computable outward moduli.
seed_details.destination_search: The generic uniform-size literature does not provide exact finite-sample termination for real-exponential coverage surfaces or mixed-integer interval policies.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic drifting-subsequence results because compactness always yields a bad convergent subsequence.
seed_details.rebuttal: Compactness detects failure but supplies neither a finite cover nor a stopping rule at exact contacts; effectiveness is the missing theorem.

seed_details.title: Frontier between worst-case honesty and integrated discrete optimality
seed_details.anchor_location: Abstract and main single-parameter optimality criterion, Statistics and Probability Letters 83, pp. 297--303
seed_details.live_opportunity: Determine when an interval optimized under integrated coverage and length remains admissible under uniform causal-panel honesty, and quantify the regime of divergence.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is replacing integration over one parameter by the supremum over a multidimensional nuisance and observed design.
seed_details.destination_search: The located paper optimizes average coverage and average expected length in one-parameter discrete families; it does not establish a worst-nuisance frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The criteria differ by definition, so any divergence result is merely terminological.
seed_details.rebuttal: A nontrivial seed would need an observable intensity frontier and an optimizer equivalence theorem; the present evidence does not yet support both directions.

seed_details.title: Efficient proportional target after fixed-effect averaging
seed_details.live_opportunity: Derive the efficient influence vector for the counterfactual-share proportional effect in the exact aggregate Poisson experiment and compare it with regular fixed-\(T\) fixed-effect averages.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is the delta-method expansion for a cross-sectional fixed-effect average; it becomes orthogonal projection of treated totals on the untreated row-plus-time score space.
seed_details.destination_search: Martin derives regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotic normality for fixed-effect averages, but the located literature does not compute the exact aggregate-Poisson efficiency bound for the staggered proportional ratio.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Martin's Theorem 2 by applying the delta method to a ratio.
seed_details.rebuttal: Martin's sampling model and estimand differ; the proposed variance requires profiling normalized cohort-time nuisance and is load-bearing for minimax risk transfer, though it is strongest as part of the bridge rather than alone.

literature_map.settled: Bayes--minimax duality, finite-support prior games, scalar exact-Poisson endpoint algorithms, and qualitative uniform-size arguments by drifting subsequences are settled in their respective models.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located result gives a deterministic finite certificate simultaneously uniform over a share simplex, a compact intensity interval, and multidimensional normalized Poisson nuisance while preserving connected actions and an integer lower witness.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Schafer and Stark prove stochastic convergence to a finite-prior game, not a finite stopping theorem for continuum honesty; Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger provide qualitative subsequence reductions, not effective exact-Poisson covers.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The setup and motivation follow Moreau-Kastler's move from nonlinear aggregation to a specific proportional estimand. The method adapts Schafer--Stark finite games, Kabaila--Byrne count enumeration, and Andrews--Cheng--Guggenberger contact-sequence control.

literature_map.settled: Expected-measure minimax duality is settled for general dominated experiments; auxiliary-uniform atom splitting is settled for scalar binomial intervals; the proportional imputation target is publicly specified for staggered PPML.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located result calculates the deterministic connected-interval value or its randomized-kernel convexification for the counterfactual-share-weighted staggered Poisson experiment.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Evans, Hansen, and Stark do not specialize their duality to this causal nuisance geometry, and Kabaila's scalar atom ordering does not survive the multivariate target map.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The zero-atom argument adapts the test-inversion view of Evans--Hansen--Stark and the probability-atom splitting move of Kabaila, while the target follows Moreau-Kastler's equation (3.14).

literature_map.settled: Global Poisson--Gaussian equivalence is settled for positive smooth nonparametric intensities; fixed-\(T\) pooled Poisson inference and fixed-effect-average normality are settled under regular high-information sampling; bounded-normal minimax expected measure is characterized in restricted location models.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No located theorem transfers worst-nuisance connected-interval length for the normalized staggered Poisson proportional target or identifies its least-favorable efficient direction.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang treat a nonparametric process rather than this profiled finite experiment; Wooldridge and Martin provide pointwise regular inference rather than convergence of a minimax confidence game.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The method adapts explicit two-sided experiment comparison from Brown--Carter--Low--Zhang and the fixed-\(T\) estimation arc of Wooldridge and Martin, then closes the limit with Evans--Hansen--Stark's bounded-location game.

novelty_justification: The flagship comparator is Schafer and Stark (2009): Theorem 6 and the Conclusion control finite-prior and off-support Monte Carlo approximations, but they do not output a deterministic finite proof of coverage over continuous observed shares and nuisance, do not terminate by an exact acceptance predicate at nominal contacts, and do not preserve a complete integer lower witness. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, is the uniformity comparator: its drifting-subsequence reduction is qualitative and asymptotic, whereas the stated open theorem requires a finite rational polyhedral cover, outward-rounded Poisson and target-membership enclosures, and a replayable verifier over every share and calibrated intensity. The structured comparator promises therefore match both papers to Open-ended Question 1 as strict finite verified strengthenings. Moreau-Kastler's equation (3.14) target and the Kabaila--Byrne homogeneous known-mass reduction are explicitly setup and sanity material, not novelty roots. The exact low-intensity frontier, randomized gap, zero-atom bound, and efficient-Gaussian bridge remain the analytic endpoints that the certificate must join.
